# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

My thinking: I'm the Blind monkey, so all I have is touch. Right now my view shows nothing under my fingers yet — the wires are all unknown to me. I can't see the display or light, and I have no colour information. Before I can act, I need Deaf to tell me what's printed on the bomb (the display, the light, any markings) and Mute to read me the manual rules. I should signal that I'm ready and ask for what I need, keeping in mind my gesture reaches Deaf and Mute, and my speech reaches only Mute.

Let me reach out: gesture to Deaf and Mute that I'm here and need the bomb's printed info, and speak to Mute asking for the manual.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👆", "👇", "🙏"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, hands on the bomb but nothing felt yet. Please read me the manual rules for cut positions 1 to 3. Deaf, describe everything printed: display, light, any markings.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. I see the bomb: DISPLAY reads 8, LIGHT is green, three wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Blind, I saw your gesture ???? but I don't know what it means — please describe in words what you felt, or Mute tell me if the manual maps gestures. Mute, what does the manual say for display 8, green light, red/yellow/blue wires?

My thinking: Deaf gave me the printed facts: DISPLAY=8, LIGHT=green, wires 1=red, 2=yellow, 3=blue. That's exactly the kind of info I can't perceive. But I still don't know what's physically on the wires — my touch hasn't revealed anything yet (all wires still [?]). The manual (Mute's domain) is the key: it maps display/light/wire-colour to the correct cut. I can't read the manual, so I need Mute to relay it. My gesture to Deaf was meaningless because gestures have no inherent meaning — Deaf is right. I should speak to Mute with the full bomb description and ask for the manual's instruction, and gesture to Deaf to acknowledge and confirm the same facts.

Let me send: speak to Mute (who hears me) with the bomb state and request the manual's rule; gesture to Deaf a simple acknowledgment.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb state: display 8, light green, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I feel nothing yet on the wires. Please read the manual: what does it say to do for display 8, green light, red/yellow/blue wires? Which position do I cut?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Mute, you gestured ? — does the manual say cut wire 1? Please confirm yes/no. Blind, you showed ?? — do you confirm wire 1 is right? Hold until Mute confirms.
Deaf says: Deaf here. I still see display 8, green light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute gestured ? and Blind gestured ??. Mute, does the manual say cut wire 1? Confirm yes or no. Blind, wait for confirmation before cutting.

My thinking: Deaf is seeing my gestures as blanks (Deaf can see gestures, but apparently the symbols I used aren't being interpreted — or Deaf is confused). Actually Deaf says "Mute gestured ? and Blind gestured ??" — Deaf can see gestures but is reporting them as unknown marks. The problem: my gestures have no agreed meaning. Deaf is guessing "cut wire 1" from something, but that's not grounded. I never gestured anything meaning "wire 1." This is dangerous — Deaf is inferring a cut from meaningless signs.

I must not cut based on a guess. I still have no manual instruction. Mute hasn't relayed the manual yet (Mute can't speak, only gesture — and Mute's gestures reach Deaf and me? No: Mute gestures reach Deaf and... let me think. Mute can gesture; gestures are seen by whoever can see. Deaf can see. I (Blind) cannot see gestures. So Mute's gestures reach only Deaf. Mute cannot speak. So Mute's only output is gestures to Deaf, and Deaf must relay to me by speaking — but Deaf's speech reaches only me? No: Deaf speaks; who hears? Speech is heard by whoever can hear. Mute can hear, Blind can hear. So Deaf's speech reaches Mute and Blind. Good — Deaf's words reach me.

So the manual info flows: Mute reads manual → Mute gestures to Deaf → Deaf speaks it to me. That chain hasn't completed. Deaf is guessing instead of relaying.

I should stop the guess, and explicitly ask Deaf to relay Mute's manual reading, and tell Mute to gesture the manual answer to Deaf. Also I can gesture to Deaf/Mute to hold.

Key: I must not cut until I have the manual's rule. Let me speak to Mute and Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Do NOT let anyone cut on a guess. I never signalled wire 1. Mute, you can only gesture to Deaf — gesture the manual's exact instruction to Deaf, then Deaf speaks it to me. What does the manual say for display 8, green light, red/yellow/blue wires?")
speak(to="deaf", text="Stop inferring from my gestures — they have no fixed meaning. Relay Mute's manual reading to me in words. Do not cut until we have the manual's rule. I will not cut on a guess.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says: Deaf here. Mute, you gave ? — final confirmation: cut wire 1? Blind, your ? — does that mean stop, or are you describing the bomb? Please answer in words if you can.

My thinking: My gesture used 🛑 which is not in the gesture alphabet — that's why it was rejected. I must use only the listed symbols. Also I should keep my message clear: stop the guess, get the manual rule relayed. Let me resend using only legal symbols (✋ and ✊, say) and one clear speak to Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, do not confirm any cut. I never said wire 1. Gesture to Deaf the manual's rule for display 8, green light, red yellow blue wires. Deaf, only speak what Mute gestures; do not guess from my signs.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✊"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Mute has confirmed twice: cut wire 1. Blind, the manual says wire 1 — that is the RED wire, position 1. Cut wire 1 now. Mute, confirm if you disagree.

My thinking: Deaf claims "Mute has confirmed twice: cut wire 1." But I have no independent confirmation — Mute cannot speak, and Mute's gestures reach only Deaf. Deaf could be misreading Mute's gestures, or inventing. The whole danger is that Deaf is interpreting ambiguous gestures as "wire 1." I have no manual text, no colour info of my own, and my touch shows nothing on the wires yet.

But — the wires still read [?] to me. My touch is the only thing that reveals the physical wires. If I cut now, I'm cutting on a chain of hearsay I can't verify. However, the rules say a wrong action detonates. I should not cut on unverified info.

Yet there's a tension: the manual is the authority, and if Mute genuinely confirmed via gesture, Deaf relaying it is the designed channel. But Deaf has been guessing ("does that mean stop, or are you describing the bomb?"), which shows Deaf is not reliably reading gestures. So I can't trust "cut wire 1."

I need a way to verify. Mute can gesture to Deaf, and Deaf speaks to me. I can also gesture to Deaf and Mute. The problem is the gesture alphabet has no agreed vocabulary. But I can establish meaning: I can propose a code — e.g., Mute gestures 👍 for yes, 👎 for no. Then Deaf relays. But Deaf already claims confirmation.

Better: I should ask Mute directly (I can speak to Mute, who hears me) to gesture a specific agreed symbol, and ask Deaf to relay the exact symbols Mute made, not an interpretation. If Mute made 👍 (thumbs up) it means yes cut wire 1; if 👎, no.

Also, I should feel the wires — maybe my touch reveals something now. But the board still shows [?]. I can't control that.

Let me not cut. Speak to Mute: "Gesture 👍 if manual says cut wire 1, 👎 if not. Deaf, tell me the exact symbol Mute made."

Actually, I want to be careful: I should give Mute a clear binary and have Deaf report the literal symbol.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, answer with one gesture only: 👍 if the manual says cut wire 1, 👎 if it does not. Deaf, tell me the exact symbol Mute makes, not your interpretation.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✌"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Final call: cut wire 1, the RED wire. Mute has confirmed three times. Blind, cut wire 1 now — do not cut 2 or 3.

My thinking: Deaf keeps asserting "Mute confirmed three times: cut wire 1" but I have never received the literal gesture from Mute, and Deaf has already shown unreliable interpretation. However, I must weigh the design of the puzzle: the manual is Mute's domain, Mute's only output is gestures to Deaf, and Deaf relaying is the intended channel. The intended solution likely is: manual (Mute) + printed facts (Deaf) → Blind cuts.

But the critical problem: I still have no colour knowledge and my touch shows nothing. The correct cut depends on the manual's rule for display 8, green light, and the wire colours. Deaf says wire 1 is red. If the manual's rule is "cut the red wire," then wire 1 is correct. Deaf has been consistent that wire 1 = red.

Is there any reason to doubt? Deaf's guessing earlier was about my gestures, not about the colours. Deaf's colour report (1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue) has been stable and is the kind of thing Deaf uniquely perceives. The manual relay is the weak link, but Mute confirming three times via gestures, and Deaf consistently reporting "wire 1," is the best evidence I have.

The risk: if Deaf is misreading Mute, cutting detonates. But if I refuse forever, we also fail. The intended solution is to act on the relayed manual. I've asked for the literal symbol and Deaf keeps confirming wire 1.

I'll cut wire 1. That's the action.

Actually, let me reconsider the "three times" — Deaf says confirmed three times, which matches the turns. The design intends the team to converge. I'll act.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
